items.title: Grealish dropped by Everton after breaching club discipline
items.excerpt: Everton said Jack Grealish was unavailable for their Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against Newcastle 'due to a breach of club discipline'.
body: Everton said Jack Grealish was unavailable for their Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against Newcastle 'due to a breach of club discipline'.

Grealish, who is on loan from Manchester City, missed Saturday's defeat at Arsenal due to illness but had started Everton's previous three Premier League matches against Ipswich, Hull City and Chelsea.

He was dropped by manager David Moyes for their cup tie at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday night after reportedly missing a training session. Transfer Centre LIVE! | Latest on YOUR PL club! Premier League fixtures & scores | FREE PL highlights ▶️

items.excerpt: Manchester City remain winless in this season's Women's Champions League after Tara Elimbi Gilbert's late strike earned Paris Saint-Germain a 1-1 draw at the Joie Stadium.
body: Manchester City remain winless in this season's Women's Champions League after Tara Elimbi Gilbert's late strike earned Paris Saint-Germain a 1-1 draw at the Joie Stadium.

Andree Jeglertz's side had appeared to be on course for a much-needed victory when Khadija Shaw - fresh from finishing third in this week's Ballon d'Or - converted an 85th-minute penalty to finally make the breakthrough against stubborn opponents, the Jamaica striker's 10th goal in her last 10 outings.

However, the hosts - unbeaten so far this season - then switched off to allow Gilbert to level just three minutes later to put in jeopardy their hopes of finishing in the top four of the new league phase, and with it automatic qualification for the quarter-finals without needing to go through the play-offs. items.title: It's been 616 days: Can Spurs finally win three in a row?
items.excerpt: By the time Saturday rolls around, it will have been 616 days since Tottenham last won three Premier League games on the bounce. Three different managers have come and gone since the feat was last achieved, none able to steer Spurs to a str…
body: By the time Saturday rolls around, it will have been 616 days since Tottenham last won three Premier League games on the bounce. Three different managers have come and gone since the feat was last achieved, none able to steer Spurs to a streak of more than two.

Roberto De Zerbi is the latest boss to try his hand at the hat-trick. Wins over Coventry City and Chelsea have preceded this weekend's meeting with Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports . The elusive treble is within reach.

To right such a wrong would be a huge stepping stone for Spurs under De Zerbi. Not only would the result propel them into the top half of the table, but its potential to heal the wounded Spurs psyche would surely be invaluable.

Dr Tottenham have long been craving a healer of their own. A manager who is able to match stylistic promise with sound leadership. Many thought the pursuit of a fiery Italian known to be volatile in previous roles was a high-risk appointment, and yet the gamble had obvious growth potential. A way back from anonymity. items.title: Hay scores twice as Dundee send Killie bottom
items.excerpt: Ash Hay piled more pressure on Kilmarnock boss Neil McCann after netting a late brace to earn Dundee a 3-1 win at Dens Park in the William Hill Premiership.
body: Ash Hay piled more pressure on Kilmarnock boss Neil McCann after netting a late brace to earn Dundee a 3-1 win at Dens Park in the William Hill Premiership.
The Dark Blues took the lead in the first half through Joe Bevan but Killie drew level thanks to a Joe Hugill penalty with 15 minutes left.
However, Dundee snatched all three points late on with Hay netting a double. The win lifts the Dark Blues up to fourth while Killie dropped to the bottom of the table.
The hosts made just one change to the team that was beaten at St Mirren on Saturday, with former Killie defender Joe Wright coming in for the injured Owen Bevan.

items.title: Krauhaus nets only goal as Falkirk beat Aberdeen
items.excerpt: Substitute Ben Krauhaus netted the only goal of a low-key match at Pittodrie as Falkirk overcame lacklustre Aberdeen to move into the top half of the William Hill Premiership table.
body: Substitute Ben Krauhaus netted the only goal of a low-key match at Pittodrie as Falkirk overcame lacklustre Aberdeen to move into the top half of the William Hill Premiership table.
The on-loan Brentford midfielder netted just eight minutes after entering the fray, and his side-footed effort from the centre of the penalty area would prove decisive.

Separated by a point before the match, both teams had designs on climbing into the top six, with virus-hit Aberdeen having lost to Dundee United at the weekend to drop to ninth, while Falkirk's 3-0 win over Kilmarnock had them sat in seventh.

The Dons made two changes to the side that fell 3-2 at Tannadice, Dan Happe returning in place of Jack Milne, while Lewis Smith took over from the injured Connor Ronan. items.title: Motherwell end losing run but miss out on St Johnstone win
items.excerpt: Motherwell ended a six-match losing streak but manager Alfred Johansson was denied a much-needed win by Josh Campbell’s stoppage-time equaliser for St Johnstone.
body: Motherwell ended a six-match losing streak but manager Alfred Johansson was denied a much-needed win by Josh Campbell’s stoppage-time equaliser for St Johnstone.

The Swede had presided over Motherwell's worst losing run since 2003 and the 2-2 draw would have felt like a body blow given the Steelmen made a strong recovery from Taylor Steven's opener against the run of play.
A virtuoso goal from Ibrahim Said brought the visitors level and they seized the initiative with Tawanda Maswanhise netting early in the second half.

Motherwell looked set to mark the 10th anniversary of the club going into fan ownership with three points but they were left with just one win in 12 games when Campbell rose unchallenged in a crowded penalty box to head home Logan Chalmers' cross. items.title: Hibs climb off foot of the table in St Mirren draw
items.excerpt: Hibernian moved off the foot of the Scottish Premiership table as they drew 1-1 at St Mirren to earn Marink Reedijk his first point as manager.
body: Hibernian moved off the foot of the Scottish Premiership table as they drew 1-1 at St Mirren to earn Marink Reedijk his first point as manager.
Marko Ivezic's second-goal put Hibs ahead in Paisley but it was cancelled out by Jason Kerr's own goal.
The draw was enough for Reedijk to finally get off the mark at the fourth attempt.

It was a scrappy match of few chances until late on when both sides had chances to earn the victory but could not take them, with Hibernian goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger doing well to deny StMirren's Jake Young. items.title: Man City dump Brighton out of Carabao Cup after shoot-out victory
items.excerpt: Carabao Cup holders Manchester City needed penalties to progress past Brighton and into the quarter-finals after battling from behind to draw the game 2-2 at the Etihad.
body: Carabao Cup holders Manchester City needed penalties to progress past Brighton and into the quarter-finals after battling from behind to draw the game 2-2 at the Etihad.

Enzo Maresca's side never led on the night but scored four of their five penalties to win the deciding shoot-out 4-3, with Rayan Cherki striking the winner and Geronimo Rulli denying both Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk.

Brighton, the better side for the majority, will consider themselves unlucky to be dumped out of a competition Fabian Hurzeler had earlier professed to want to win. But City stuck to task and eventually prevailed on penalties - Hurzeler gets his chance to enact revenge when the two sides meet again in the Premier League on Saturday.
